requirement_text.REQ-441:
Implements the real mail adapter behind the notifier PORT that REQ-437
specifies (Letflow.LoginDiscovery.Notifier, @callback
deliver_tenant_list/2, design s13) and replaces its non-delivering
default for deployments that enable the feature. REQUIRED before the
email-first feature flag can be enabled outside dev (REQ-444's boot
refusal treats the non-delivering Noop adapter as not real, and REQ-444
depends_on this entry). Provider-agnostic: the port is the abstraction;
SMTP is the first adapter. SECURITY-REVIEWER is a named hard gate (new
external egress, INV-4 credentials, INV-8, INV-9, INV-5 uniformity).

FIRST STEP, before any implementation (WF-02): a CODE-DESIGNER pass
that chooses the mail library, records the choice as a decision record
under docs/migration/decisions/ and designs the adapter, its
configuration and its failure handling. This entry adds a runtime
dependency, so the library choice is a decision, not an implementation
detail; ELIXIR-DEV does not start until that design has passed
CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR.

NOTE ONLY, out of scope: the same adapter is expected to serve
invitations and password recovery later. Nothing here builds those, and
the port is not widened for them; a later requirement may add
callbacks.

BUILDS:
1. An SMTP adapter module implementing the REQ-437 notifier behaviour
(for example Letflow.LoginDiscovery.Notifier.Smtp), plus whatever
mailer module the chosen library needs. Library choice (proposal:
Swoosh with its SMTP adapter over gen_smtp; alternatives Bamboo or a
bare gen_smtp) is made by CODE-DESIGNER and recorded as a decision
record; mix.exs gains only that dependency. The hex dependency needs
network for mix deps.get; if this environment cannot fetch it, say so
explicitly rather than guessing.
2. Configuration by environment reference only (INV-4, no secret in the
repository): LETFLOW_MAIL_ADAPTER (the adapter selector; unset or
unknown keeps the Noop default, unknown value raises at boot),
LETFLOW_SMTP_HOST, LETFLOW_SMTP_PORT, LETFLOW_SMTP_USERNAME,
LETFLOW_SMTP_PASSWORD, LETFLOW_SMTP_TLS (verified TLS by default;
plaintext only when explicitly set and never in :prod), LETFLOW_MAIL_FROM
and the deployment base URL for any link (INV-9). Read once at boot in
config/runtime.exs; with the adapter selected, a missing host,
credentials or sender raises at boot with a message that echoes no
value; .env.example (and deploy/.env.example) document the names with no
working value. The password is never logged, never in a struct field
that is inspected or serialised, and never in a crash report.
3. UNIFORM RESPONSE WHATEVER THE DELIVERY RESULT: delivery runs in the
notifier task off the request path (REQ-437 item 5). A successful send,
an SMTP rejection, a timeout, a connection or TLS failure and a raise
all leave the HTTP status, headers and body byte-identical and add no
per-request signal. Failure handling: no automatic retry in this
requirement (a retry loop is an email-bombing amplifier; the per-address
:send bucket of REQ-436 is consumed once per attempt, success or
failure); the failure is recorded only as a non-identifying counter
event [:letflow, :login_discovery, :notifier] with a single metadata
key outcome in {:delivered, :failed, :skipped}, and a fixed log line
carrying no address, tenant, slug, SMTP reply text or exception text.
4. A fixed message template (design s13 'message contract'): the only
request-derived text is the recipient address; tenant slugs and display
names appear as plain text; any link is built from the deployment base
URL and the slug URL-encoded, never from tenant-controlled URL text; no
HTML from tenant text (plain-text body, or HTML with all interpolated
values escaped); subject and body fixed strings.
5. A capturing test adapter under test/support/ that records
(recipient, tenants) calls and can be set to return {:error, _}, raise,
exit or sleep. If REQ-437's test double already provides this, reuse it
and add nothing; do not duplicate it.
6. ADAPTER SELECTION KEY: config/runtime.exs maps LETFLOW_MAIL_ADAPTER
onto the application-env key `config :letflow,
Letflow.LoginDiscovery.Notifier, adapter: <module>` (design s13; REQ-437
defines the key with the Noop default). A selected Smtp adapter with
incomplete configuration refuses to boot (item 2). The enablement gate
that treats Smtp as a real adapter is REQ-444, not built here.

OPEN QUESTIONS: ["OPEN, decision needed (CODE-DESIGNER, recorded in docs/migration/decisions/): the mail library and, if an external transactional provider is preferred later, the second adapter. SMTP is first by BA decision D-B.", "EXTERNAL dependency, not in this repository: the ai-dala-infra secrets inventory needs entries for the SMTP credentials (LETFLOW_SMTP_USERNAME / LETFLOW_SMTP_PASSWORD) and the chosen SMTP relay per environment (0042 OQ-4 asked who owns the credentials: the platform operator). Recorded, not edited from here.", "OPEN, only remaining user/legal decision of the series (0042 OQ-3, decision 0043 D-D): the feature stays off outside dev until a named person confirms the lawful basis and controller; this entry makes the mail adapter real but does not lift that gate. Sender domain SPF/DKIM/DMARC alignment is an infrastructure action outside this repository.", "SMTP replies can reveal whether a mailbox exists (a synchronous rejection). This is safe only because the delivery result never reaches the HTTP response; the counters carry no address. Confirm with SECURITY-REVIEWER that the :failed counter's rate is not itself an oracle an operator-visible dashboard could expose per address (it carries no per-address dimension).", "Keycloak Organizations: DEFERRED (BA decision D-G); not relevant to this entry."]

task.description: WF-02 step 03b (TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR), hard gate on TEST-DESIGNER for REQ-441 (spec test/specs/REQ-441.md; tests listed there; handoff step-03-test-designer.json). Verify: every one of the 10 acceptance criteria has a runnable test asserting what the criterion says (not weaker); no skipped/excluded tests (@tag :skip, @moduletag :skip, ExUnit exclude); fixtures isolated and self-sufficient (async-safety of Application env / named processes / ports; partitions); no real network egress (sink in-process, loopback only); no value assigned to LETFLOW_SMTP_* secrets in the repo beyond runtime-only fake values in test code; the findings of step-01c, 02c, 02d are covered (stale mix.exs guard replaced by content assertion; AC6 grep guard; F4; allow_test_cacerts; F9 capacity; encoder tests; AC8 mail_adapter variable equality). Independently re-run a scoped subset yourself with MIX_ENV=test MIX_TEST_PARTITION=441i (e.g. test/letflow/login_discovery/notifier/ and test/letflow/mail_runtime_config_test.exs and test/letflow/req441_source_guards_test.exs) and spot-mutate at most two shipped behaviours to confirm tests fail (restore via `git checkout -- <file>` ONLY after confirming `git status` shows nothing else uncommitted; the tree is committed so this is safe; never use git stash/reset). Do not edit tests or lib; report required fixes. Write the verdict into this handoff result (PASS/FAIL, numbered findings, next_action TEST-RUNNER or TEST-DESIGNER), COMPLETED with real UTC completed_at >= started_at; run mix letflow.lint_handoffs.
acceptance_criteria: the Smtp adapter implements Letflow.LoginDiscovery.Notifier (a Mox-style or behaviour-conformance test shows the callbacks and return shapes match REQ-437's port exactly); the port itself is not changed

delivery against a local SMTP sink started by the test (an in-process listener, no network egress): a multi-tenant address's notifier task sends exactly one message whose recipient is the typed address and whose body lists the active tenants' slugs and display names as plain text with a link built from the configured base URL; the sink receives no other recipient

uniform response: through the real Letflow.Routers.LoginDiscovery chain, the response bytes for the same multi-tenant POST are byte-identical when the adapter succeeds, returns {:error, _}, raises, exits, times out, and when the SMTP sink refuses the recipient, refuses the connection, or fails TLS; the request process stays alive; status, headers and body compared directly

failure handling: after a failed attempt the per-address :send bucket is consumed (a second attempt inside the interval is skipped, not retried); no retry process is started (a grep guard shows no retry loop or Process.send_after on the delivery path); the [:letflow, :login_discovery, :notifier] event is emitted once per attempt with metadata exactly %{outcome: _}

no leak: the full capture_log(level: :debug) output across the success and every failure case above contains no email address, no tenant slug or display name, no SMTP reply text, no password and no exception message text; the typed email is placed in the exception message of the raising double to prove it (design s13 C-4 form); a grep guard shows no start_child/Task.start/spawn with an MFA or argument-list form under lib/letflow/login_discovery/

no secret in the repository: a grep guard over the tracked tree finds no value assigned to LETFLOW_SMTP_PASSWORD or LETFLOW_SMTP_USERNAME outside the variable names in .env.example/docs, and .env.example names the variables with no working value; quoted

boot configuration tested (config/runtime.exs evaluated with a controlled environment): LETFLOW_MAIL_ADAPTER unset keeps Noop; unknown value raises; smtp selected with a missing host, port, sender or credentials raises with a message containing none of the values; a complete configuration boots; plaintext TLS mode raises in :prod

adapter selection: LETFLOW_MAIL_ADAPTER=smtp sets the application-env key `config :letflow, Letflow.LoginDiscovery.Notifier, adapter:` to the Smtp module (and unset leaves Noop), asserted from the evaluated runtime config; this is the same key the enablement gate of REQ-444 reads (the gate itself, and its test with the Smtp module, belong to REQ-444, which depends_on this entry)

message template: subject and body are fixed strings; a tenant display name containing markup, a newline or a URL is rendered as inert text and produces no extra header and no link other than the configured-base-URL link (header-injection and link-injection test)

`mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, `mix format --check-formatted`, `mix test` for the touched areas and `mix letflow.check_boundaries` pass, real output quoted; the SECURITY-REVIEWER verdict is recorded against INV-4, INV-5, INV-8 and INV-9

result.summary: PASS. All 10 acceptance criteria map to runnable, unskipped tests (no @tag/@moduletag :skip, no TODO, no ExUnit exclude covering them; test_helper excludes only :keycloak/:wasm_hang/:lua_wallclock_race). Independent runs with MIX_ENV=test MIX_TEST_PARTITION=441i: (a) notifier/ dir + mail_runtime_config_test + req441_source_guards_test + no_smtp_secret_guard_test = 303 passed, exit 0; (b) dispatch_notifier_event_test + notifier_no_leak_test + login_discovery_notifier_uniform_test + login_discovery_test + dispatch_test = 151 passed, exit 0. Isolation: every ExUnit.Case touching Application env/named processes/ports is async: false (only the pure message test, secret-guard and source-guard tests are async: true); sink binds 127.0.0.1 with an OS-assigned port, no outbound egress; SMTP credentials appear only as runtime-built fake values via System.put_env. Re-grep of the tracked tree finds no value assigned to LETFLOW_SMTP_USERNAME/PASSWORD in code or .env files (only prose/quoted-pattern mentions in handoff and design docs, which the guard's refined shapes deliberately ignore). Prior-gate findings covered: stale mix.exs git-diff guard replaced by content assertion (login_discovery_test.exs:434); AC6 grep guard; F4 telemetry-handler guard; allow_test_cacerts compile-time gate guard; F9 capacity (12 requests at burst 5, 201 submits vs max_concurrent); encoder tests (REVIEWER finding 3); AC8 mail_adapter variable equality. Mutants applied by me (spec's code-already-existed fail-first rule): MUTANT A transport.ex line 76 'retries: 0' -> 'retries: 3' run against dispatch_notifier_event_test + smtp_test + req441_source_guards_test: 56/63 passed, 7 failed (retries guard in SR, bucket-after-drop, no-retry-on-drop, EV retry grep guard, 3 SM TLS/STARTTLS single-attempt tests). MUTANT B message.ex line 164 URI.encode_www_form(slug) -> raw slug run against smtp_message_test + smtp_encoder_test: 104/112 passed, 8 failed (hostile-slug cases, tenant_link encoding, property, two wire-level injection tests). Both reverted with git checkout -- <file>; 'git status --porcelain lib/ test/ config/ mix.exs' empty and re-run of message+encoder+source-guard tests = 124 passed. Unmodified tree only untracked letflow-3.code-workspace (pre-existing, not mine). Not re-run by me: full suite, compile/format/boundaries (AC10 non-ExUnit parts belong to TEST-RUNNER).

issues.detail: 1. Mutation evidence is my own measured counts (A: 7 of 63 failed; B: 8 of 112 failed), not copied from the spec's M1/M7 rows.
2. AC10's compile --warnings-as-errors, format --check-formatted, check_boundaries and the SECURITY-REVIEWER record (step-02c PASS) are not ExUnit tests; TEST-RUNNER must quote real output for them.
